text:
The officer on the screen is wearing an unmarked pressure suit. Your transponder record appears beside a damage report.

"$entity.catchrelease_harpoonHitmanVictim. $entity.catchrelease_harpoonHitmanOrigin. You hit them with $entity.catchrelease_harpoonHitmanOffence."

The officer waits while your comms officer verifies the record.

"They've paid us to deal with you. Anything you'd like to say before we start?"

The officer on the screen is wearing an unmarked pressure suit. Your transponder record appears beside a damage report.

"You hit $entity.catchrelease_harpoonHitmanVictim with $entity.catchrelease_harpoonHitmanOffence in $entity.catchrelease_harpoonHitmanOrigin. They hired us."

Your comms officer points out that the client is no longer around to collect.

"Payment cleared before that happened. We still have a contract."

The officer checks a clause in the contract.

"Cancellation, damages, legal fees. $entity.catchrelease_harpoonHitmanBribeDGS credits, paid now. We both walk away."

The transfer clears. The officer closes your file.

"Contract cancelled. Try not to harpoon someone important, next time."

Your call reaches a damage-control compartment. Someone reads out your transponder code.

"Is this yours?"

An image of the recovered harpoon head appears. Your comms officer confirms that it is fishing equipment.

"Yes, we'd worked that out. What were you trying to catch?"

"Hegemony Navy. $PersonRank $personName."

An incident report appears on your display.

"We've recovered your projectile. Naval Intelligence will examine it. You can apply for a receipt at a military office; quote the number on that report."

$HeOrShe looks up.

"That isn't an invitation to come and collect it."

"We have your transponder particulars, Captain. Repairs, lost operating time, removal and disposal will be billed to you. Legal is still deciding how to classify the projectile."

$PersonRank $personName sends the invoice without waiting for an answer. "I don't expect their decision to reduce the amount."
$PersonRank $personName looks at the damage feed. Then at you. "Whatever purpose that machine was built for, captain, this was not it."

The speaker has the recovered ROD head on the table behind them.

"Accident?" They jab a finger toward it. "You cast Moloch's iron through a ship full of Ludd's children and call it an accident?"

Someone off-screen shouts assent.

"Fire another. See what answer you get."

$personName turns the recovered projectile toward the camera. "You hooked us."

The pirate grins despite everything. "Actually hooked us." Then the grin goes away. "Don't do it again."

"You fired on a vessel of the Sindrian Diktat. I am required to establish whether the act was deliberate."

$PersonRank $personName sends an incident notice. "For your sake, I have entered it as an accident. Do not give me cause to amend that finding."

$PersonRank $personName is searching through a set of regulations.

"Negligent discharge, damage to an associated hull... there's a recovery-equipment provision somewhere."

$HeOrShe gives up looking.

"I will find the appropriate charge, captain. Don't mistake a gap in the index for permission."
"You put a hole in us with fishing gear." $personName rubs the bridge of $hisOrHer nose. "I have to explain that sentence to a yardmaster."

text:
"We've received a damage claim against your fleet, Captain. I'm sending you the report."

An image of the recovered harpoon head is attached to an assessment for $entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits.

"Pay the repair and we'll record it as negligent discharge. Keep that thing pointed away from traffic."

"Cut your drive, Captain. We're following up a weapons-discharge report. You may settle the assessed damages of $entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits now. A further incident will be treated as a deliberate attack."

"Corporate security. Your fleet damaged Tri-Tachyon property. I'm authorized to collect $entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits, including recovery costs and lost operating time. Shall we close the claim?"

"Peace be with you. Cut your drive."

$PersonRank $personName looks at the damage report.

"You damaged a crewed vessel with equipment no prudent captain should point at one."

"The repair is $entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits."

"Pay the people whose hull you opened."

"You put Moloch's iron through a ship full of people and now you want this treated as an accident?"

The claim figure appears.

"$entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits. Pay it."

A finger jabs at the recovered-hardware image.

"Then throw that thing out an airlock."

"Hold up." $PersonName grins. "Heard you put a fishing harpoon through somebody's plating. I'd have liked to see that. Unfortunately for you, they pay us to take an interest. $entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS and we're even."

"You have damaged a vessel under Sindrian protection. The State is prepared to accept $entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits in settlement."

$PersonRank $personName transmits the penalty notice. "This is a courtesy, Captain. A second discharge will not receive the same consideration."

"Damage to an associated hull through negligent operation of heavy recovery equipment. $entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits."

$PersonRank $personName waits for an acknowledgment. "Yes, I understand it was fishing equipment. Have you seen the damage?"

"Ease off, Captain. Someone you harpooned has filed a claim. They've sent us the yard estimate: $entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits. I'm sure you've got an explanation, but they've still got a hole in the hull. Can we settle it?"

"We accepted your explanation last time. You're not paying your way out of this one."

The other ships begin spreading into combat formation.

$PersonRank $personName opens the channel just long enough to confirm your identity.

"Yes. That fleet."

The link closes as the other ships move to engage.
"The first incident may have been an accident. The second is deliberate." $PersonRank $personName sets the slate face down. "Weapons are authorized."
"You've done it twice. That does simplify things. Your fleet is now recorded as deliberately hostile to Tri-Tachyon assets. I expect the consequences will be considerably less routine."
$PersonRank $personName does not offer peace this time. "We took payment for the hull and said nothing about the gear that made the hole. That was a courtesy, and you have shown us what it bought."

There is no greeting. The speaker is already shouting when the channel opens.

"Again! Moloch puts a hook in your hand and you cast it into Ludd's children twice?"

Spittle marks the inside of the visor.

"Break the launcher or burn with it."
"Told you what was happening if you did it twice." The pirate stops to think about it. "I didn't, actually. My mistake."
"You were told the penalty was the favourable outcome." $PersonRank $personName closes the notice.

text: "Captain. Have you got the order? I've had another kitchen call since we last spoke."
A provisioner at the next table is calling suppliers. You have heard the same question three times now: how much can they actually deliver?

text:
"Do you supply catch? I've got kitchens asking for more than my usual boats can bring in. If you can fill this, there's $catchreleaseReward in it for you."

The provisioner passes you the order: $catchreleaseAsk. $catchreleaseDeadline
options:

text: "Good. I'll put you down for it. Contact me when you've got the full order aboard."
"All right. If you hear of anyone looking for the work, send them my way." The provisioner returns to the supplier list.
"The order's still $catchreleaseAsk. $catchreleaseDeadlineLeft I need the full lot before I can settle up."
The provisioner has the containers checked against the order before arranging your payment. "That's the lot. Good. I'll let the kitchens know they can stop calling me."
The chef answers over the noise of the kitchen. "Captain! Tell me you've got the fish. Not you, I'm talking to the captain! Put that down before you break it."

A cook in stained whites is shouting into a comm unit. "Then why did you take the bloody order?" Three ingredient cards lie beside an untouched drink. The cook stabs a finger at each one, though the supplier cannot possibly see them.

options: catchrelease_chef_ask:Talk to the cook with the ingredient cards

text:
"You catch fish? Good. My supplier's apparently taken up another profession without telling me. I'm putting $catchreleaseDish on the menu. Apparently half the station has decided they can't live without it."

The chef shoves three ingredient cards toward you. "$catchreleaseAskCap. All three. Don't bring me a hold full of one and tell me it's just as good. I know what goes in my own dish."

$catchreleaseDeadline

"$catchreleaseRewardCap for the lot. Gods know I'm not getting it from anyone else."
options:
catchrelease_chef_dish:"Why not change the dish?"
catchrelease_jobAccept:Take the order.
catchrelease_jobDecline:Decline.

text: "Good! Leave the handling tags on. Last thing I need is the prep crew arguing over which one goes where. They can argue after service, on their own bloody time."
"Then why are we having this conversation?" The chef snatches up the comm unit. "Get me your supervisor. No, I'll hold."

"$catchreleaseAskCap. All three! People are booking tables for this thing, and the head waiter keeps accepting more. I've told him we're waiting on ingredients. He says that's a kitchen matter. Wonderful. Very helpful."

$catchreleaseDeadlineLeft

The chef checks each tag and hauls the containers toward the kitchen.

"Yes! Finally! Clear that bench. Where's the prep crew?"

Somebody answers from behind the stoves.

"On a break? They've had all bloody day! Move! I've got the fish, you've got no excuses!"

The payment arrives while the chef is still shouting.
"Captain! I've been telling people about the selection we'll be offering. They're interested. What have you got for me?"
A young factor has reserved the seat opposite with an expensive sleeveless jacket. A ten-page business case is open on $hisOrHer slate; the drink beside it has barely been touched.

options: catchrelease_startup_ask:Hear the pitch from the young factor in the expensive jacket

text:
"Captain. Excellent. I was hoping to speak to someone who actually moves goods."

The factor clears the jacket off the seat. "Fish. People want a selection, but they buy whatever happens to be available. An independent captain can source the stock; a dedicated factor can develop the market. Put the two together and you have a business. I've worked through the case. The margins are very attractive."

You ask who is supplying the fish.

"That's what I wanted to discuss. Three consignments, increasing in volume. I pay on delivery. You get a dependable buyer; I establish supply."

options: 100:catchrelease_jobAccept:"All right. Let's see what you can do."

text:
"Private buyers initially. Establishments later, once they've seen what we can provide."

The factor shows you a page divided into three shaded columns. "These are conservative estimates. I've assumed most people won't buy anything."

options: catchrelease_startup_estimates:"That still leaves quite a few who will."
catchrelease_startup_customers:"Have any of them agreed to buy?"
100:catchrelease_startup_back:Go over the rest of the proposal.

text:
"Centralized purchasing, followed by direct distribution. I handle the buyers, you supply the fish. A very straightforward division of responsibilities."

"Where does the stock go?"

"Here, to me."

"And after that?"

The factor taps the pages against the table. "I'm comparing arrangements. There are costs that become clearer once you have an actual consignment to discuss. I can hardly make sensible decisions about everything in advance."

options: catchrelease_startup_costs:"So you don't know what distribution will cost."
100:catchrelease_startup_back:Go over the rest of the proposal.

text:
"Three deliveries under one agreement. Each order will be larger than the last, and worth more to you. I pay for each separately. Hand one over, and the next begins."

The first order is for $catchreleaseAsk. The payment listed beneath it is $catchreleaseReward.

"You choose the species, provided each consignment is all one kind. You can change it next time. There's no deadline."

"Good. I'll put your fleet down as our supplier."

The factor gathers the pages. "People prefer to deal with an established concern. Once the stock arrives, we'll be one."

"Of course. It won't suit everyone."

The jacket goes back on the empty chair.

The factor calls up the current order: $catchreleaseAsk.

"No deadline, as agreed. Do let me know when you're coming in, though. I want to arrange a viewing."
The factor checks the delivery against the order and arranges the agreed payment. "Excellent. I'll get this into the figures."

The factor meets your consignment with a storage clerk, who finishes explaining something and leaves.

"Apparently the storage charge begins today. I'd allowed for it from the first sale."

"That isn't usually how storage works."

"No, I understand their position. It's just a rather narrow view of the enterprise."

Your payment clears promptly. The next order is for $catchreleaseAsk, with $catchreleaseReward on delivery.

"Still, we have stock. People will take us seriously now."

"I've had inquiries," the factor announces. "Several."

Payment for the shipment clears before $heOrShe continues. "They want smaller purchases delivered individually. The carrier charges for each destination."

You suggest including that in the price.

"Yes. Once volume is sufficient, it should be a negligible expense."

The final order is for $catchreleaseAsk. The offered payment is $catchreleaseReward.
"I'm considering a wider market," the factor tells you as your final payment clears. "Local inquiries have been encouraging, but people are slow to commit."
"Captain. The specimen, I presume? I can have a porter at your berth within the hour."
A $manOrWoman in an immaculately cut coat sits beside an untouched drink. When a server tries to clear the second place, $heOrShe quietly asks that it be left.

text:
"You are the fishing captain?" The $manOrWoman moves a folded household schedule away from the spare place. "I require a live specimen for a private residence. Weight is the principal consideration. I am told it is necessary to specify that in advance."

$HeOrShe looks at the empty chair, then at you. "Do sit down, if this is likely to take some time."

"The chief butler. His personal rooms, not the household's. I attend to his appointments and purchases."

$HeOrShe waits while you make sense of that. "Will the distinction affect your ability to supply the fish?"

"His receiving room has a new tank. The specimen is to be visible from the far end."

The under-butler shows you a photograph but keeps the device on $hisOrHer side of the table. "I should mention that it is for display. The previous supplier thought we were ordering for the kitchen."

Two children have taken over a corner table with an empty bucket and a hand-drawn tournament bracket. Several names have been crossed out and written back in.

text:
"We're having a tournament!" The loud child turns a hand-drawn bracket toward you.

"But we need two more fish," says the quiet one.

"And he won't let me pick."

"Because you always pick yours first."

The loud child points at you. "You do it! You're a captain. You can make him listen."

options: 30:catchrelease_duel_terms:"What do you need me to bring?"

text:
The quiet child turns the bracket over. Rules run down the back in two different colours.

"One fish each. No swapping. Don't mess with the other person's fish."

"That means no poking," says the loud child.

"That's messing with it."

"Then write poking."

The quiet child adds it, pressing hard enough to tear the paper.

"Because he says I always take the better one," says the loud child.

"You do."

"Not always."

"You took mine out of my bucket!"

"I was looking at it." The loud child turns back to you. "You pick. Then he can't complain."

"I can still complain. I just can't swap."

text:
The Commissioner recognizes you. "$catchreleaseFightNights $catchreleaseFightNightWord supplying the fights, is it? Word gets around."

"Fancy another? We're after $catchreleaseAsk. $catchreleaseDeadline Fee's $catchreleaseReward."

The barkeeper comes over to hear your answer. "Same arrangement. Take the fee or back a fighter once the odds are up."

"You supply both fighters. I measure each against the normal size range for its species, so a big specimen counts for more than a species that just happens to be big."

The Commissioner shows you the calculations in the book. "An even pair starts at thirty-eight percent each. The rest goes to the house. You can keep the supplier's fee or wager it on either fighter. If your fighter loses, the fee is all you lose."

The barkeeper pours another drink.

"House gets whatever's left between the two. It's all written up there."

"Equal pair means thirty-eight each," the Commissioner says. "Leaves twenty-four for the house."

The bottle goes back on the shelf. "And don't hit the glass. We already replaced it once."

From the benches: "Your shift hasn't picked a winner in three fights."

"Four," somebody answers.

The Commissioner writes your name into the supplier book. "Good. $catchreleaseAsk. $catchreleaseDeadline Bring both in together; we'll weigh them, post the odds, and you can decide what to do with your fee."

"Fair enough." The Commissioner reopens the notebook.

The barkeeper calls down the bar, "Still need two for the fight!"

text: The Last Entry
Holding for catalogue filing

Expedition $entity.catchreleaseFleetExpedition has completed its survey, but one specimen entry remains open. $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName needs the requested specimen to close the entry and file the catalogue without voiding the expedition's survey classification.
The expedition will accept delivery on the following terms.
"This is the survey vessel $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName. Registry $entity.catchreleaseFleetRegistry, expedition $entity.catchreleaseFleetExpedition. Do you take specimen commissions?"

"We should have been on our way home by now. I've got one entry left in the catalogue, and we lose the expedition's survey classification if I submit it incomplete. The captain reminds me what it's costing to keep us here whenever we pass in the corridor."

The data officer sends you a commission for $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk, offering $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward.

"Can you help us finish?"

"$entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName here. Yes, the entry's still open. Have you found $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk? The captain's asked about it twice this watch."

$entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadlineLeft

The expedition staff weigh and photograph the specimen while the data officer fills in the final entry. This time the accession field has a name attached before the officer signs it.

"Accepted. I'll submit the catalogue now."

The sighting is dated $entity.catchreleaseFleetEntryDate at $entity.catchreleaseFleetCoordinates, signed $entity.catchreleaseFleetSignature.

"I can't find that name in the personnel index. Nobody by that name has served aboard $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName. I've asked the captain and checked the old rosters. If you bring in a specimen, at least I'll be able to sign for it myself."
"The catalogue's filed, Captain. I've kept the old sighting record, but your specimen has an entry of its own. We can finally get underway. Thank you."
The Escrow
Closing out the contract

Recovery vessel $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName is trying to close contract $entity.catchreleaseFleetContract. The original specimen disappeared with its carrier, but the contract allows a replacement. The skipper needs $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk before the outstanding liability grows any further.
The skipper offers the following terms for a replacement.
"Recovery vessel $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName. Skipper speaking. I've got a contract I need off my books."

"We took a contract to recover a missing shipment. Couldn't find the carrier, and now we're liable for the delivery ourselves. $entity.catchreleaseFleetLiability so far. I should have had somebody else read the thing before I signed."

The skipper sends you the replacement clause. "We can still supply the same catch. Get me $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk and I can close this before it costs us the ship. I'll pay $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward."

$entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadline

text: "Good. I'm sending you the parts of $entity.catchreleaseFleetContract that matter. Bring the catch here and I'll deal with the client."
"I'll take it. Call when you've got something; I'll get the receiving crew ready."
"All right. I've got other calls out. $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName out."

"Have you got $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk? We're still liable for $entity.catchreleaseFleetLiability, and I'd like to settle it before Legal adds anything else."

$entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadlineLeft

The skipper checks the specimen against the replacement clause and signs the receipt before letting the deck crew move it.

"Accepted. You've got your copy; I'm sending the other to the client. That should stop the charges."

"They won't give us the name. I've asked. Their legal department can reach us well enough when there's another charge to add."

The skipper opens the amendment again. "All right. I can justify it that way. $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward."

$entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadline
The Interment
Holding for interment

Burial convoy $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName needs the first species named in a guild elder's will before the appointed interment. The convoy has no fishing rig and cannot make a port stop without missing the window.
The estate will accept delivery on the following terms.
"This is the convoy master aboard $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName. We bear one of our elders to interment. May we ask a service of you, Captain?"

A guild pennant hangs behind the convoy master.

"Our elder set down their wishes for the burial while they could still put hand to paper. They asked that the first species they ever landed should accompany them. We have no rig aboard, and a port call would cost us the appointed window."

The passage from the will is sent to you. "We require $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. The estate has set aside $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward for whoever completes this duty. Will you undertake it?"

$entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadline

"The undertaking is enough. No fisher commands the catch. I will send you the elder's record; bring what it names, if you can."
"Go with our goodwill, Captain. We will ask another to undertake the duty."

"The casket remains open. We are waiting upon $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk before the company can make its farewell."

$entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadlineLeft

The convoy master receives the container with both hands. A crewman reads the species from the will; another repeats it while the catch is wrapped and marked with the elder's name.

"What was asked has been brought. Let it be witnessed."

Those gathered in the hold bow their heads.

"First catch goes with them, last catch closes the log. So it was done for those who taught us. So we do for those who follow."

The convoy master touches the seal on the will. "The species, Captain. We do not keep a fisher's first catch in a locker all their life. The elder took care to name it."

"The casket is complete. We can carry our elder onward."

The convoy master raises an open hand in farewell. "Your service will be named when the log is read. May your own closing entry be many years from now, Captain."

$entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadlineLeft

The researcher has both specimens put through the instrument set, then asks for the sequence to be repeated. The second readings are entered beside the first rather than written over them.

"That's the pair delivered. I'll arrange your payment."

"I'm sending you the results. We use the same certified mass each time; we ought to get the same reading. As you can see, we haven't. I want a reference that hasn't spent the last transit bolted into our calibration locker."

"Code $entity.catchreleaseFleetFeedstockCode. It's in the table between rendered protein stock and agricultural slurry. Nobody aboard had ever used that intake, but we checked and the fittings are there. Apparently somebody thought we'd need it."
"Printer's running. That's food taken care of." The engineer puts the drive repair schedule back up. "Now I can keep everyone on the drive."
"The printer can turn one fish into weeks of ration stock," the engineer says. "We cook it ourselves, we get dinner. I'd rather have the weeks."
A ship is broadcasting a standard distress call. Its drive plume flickers in and out as it struggles to hold position.
Fleet on a Hunt
Searching

The captain of $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName has spent eleven weeks trying to replace a specimen sold out of someone else's collection. The owner is retiring and will soon inspect it. In exchange for the missing specimen, the captain is offering the proceeds of an increasingly expensive search.
The captain's offer is recorded on the following terms.
"Captain here. If you've got a minute, I'd like to talk."
"Eleven weeks. Wrong gear, wrong places, advice from every drunk who's ever seen a fishing boat."

The captain sends an old species record. "I still haven't got $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. Bring it here and I'll give you $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward. I'm not haggling. This trip was never supposed to make money."

$entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadline

options:
0:catchrelease_fqAccept:"I'll take the job."

text: "Good. I'll send you the record for $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. Bring it here when you have it."
"Fair enough. I'll keep your payment aside. Let me know when you've found it."

"All right."

The captain closes the channel.

"Any luck with $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk? We've kept looking. Nothing yet."

$entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadlineLeft

The captain opens the container personally. There is a long inspection, with frequent glances at an old photograph.

"That's it. That'll do."

An order goes out to transfer your payment. The captain is still looking at the specimen when the crew come to take it away.

"It belonged to my old captain. I looked after the collection."

The captain closes the record. "Got into debt. Sold one. My decision. Wasn't my property."

"Now he's retiring. Wants everything packed and sent on, which means somebody's going to count it. I told myself I'd replace it before that happened. Been telling myself for eleven weeks."
"It's packed. I've told him the collection's ready to send. Thank you, Captain. I'd appreciate you keeping this between us."
Short of Quota
Filling quota

The purser aboard $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName is trying to fill a shortfall on station provisioning contract $entity.catchreleaseFleetContract. An incomplete delivery would let the station reopen the fleet's rates in arbitration. The purser can buy qualifying fish from you out of the season's remaining margin; species can be mixed.
The purser can authorize a supplemental purchase on the following terms.
"Fishing fleet $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName, purser's office. Sorry to trouble you, captain. We're short on a provisioning contract and I understand you've got fishing gear aboard."

The purser takes the call on the working deck. Someone in the background shouts a tally.

"Count it again," the purser calls back, then turns to you. "Sorry, captain. I know what the count is. I'd just rather it weren't."

"We're short on contract $entity.catchreleaseFleetContract. That's a station provisioning order. If we file short, they can send the whole thing to arbitration and start discussing our rates."

"We need $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. I can buy against the shortfall without asking the owners. $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward is as far as my authority goes."

The grade requirements follow the offer.

"Any species that meets those terms. And please check the grade. I've already had enough arguments about what ought to count."

$entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadline

0:catchrelease_fqAccept:"I'll take the job."
5:catchrelease_fqAcceptNoPromise:"I'll try. No promises." (Accept)
10:catchrelease_fqDecline:Decline.

text: "Thank you. I'm sending the grade schedule with the order. I know I'm being particular, but if it grades below that, I can't put it against the quota."
"Please try. I'll send the grade schedule. Call when you've got something I can put against the shortfall."
"Yes, understood. Sorry to take your time." The purser's eyes drop to the ledger again. "We'll keep our boats out and see what comes in. $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName out."

"Another boat's come in, but most of it graded below contract. We're still short $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. Have you got anything for us?"

$entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadlineLeft

The purser meets the transfer on the working deck with two tally clerks and the contract grade sheet.
The catch is counted and checked as it comes across.

One specimen is set aside, examined again, then returned to the accepted lot.

"There. That's the quota."

The purser checks the figure once more before signing the receipt.

"Same grounds we've fished for years. Some stopped producing. Some shifted, and now we spend the fuel finding them."

The purser shows you several old returns, all comfortably above the present quota.

"That's what the station will bring to arbitration. They'll ask what's changed aboard our ships. I've got no figure I can put against 'the fish aren't where they used to be.'"

"So I buy what's missing and hope next season is better."
"Filed complete. I've kept your grade report in case they query it. You've saved us a very unpleasant meeting, Captain. Thank you."
Hungry Fleet
Rationing

After $entity.catchreleaseFleetRationDays days of printed protein, the crew of $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName has submitted a proposed menu to command. The galley chief has been given the job of finding something worth cooking. Any species will do, provided your delivery meets the order.
The galley chief's provisioning offer is recorded on the following terms.
"Galley chief aboard $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName. I'm the cook, and command has wisely left this negotiation to me."

"Captain. I understand you fish."

The galley chief has taken over a corner of the mess for the call.

"We've been eating printed protein for $entity.catchreleaseFleetRationDays days. The crew petitioned command this morning. Very respectful. They even attached a menu."

The chief holds it up.

"I've worked in galleys for twenty years. I don't need a gunner explaining stew to me. I need something to put in the pot."

"$entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. Species doesn't matter, so long as it meets the order. I have $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward to spend."

"And if anyone asks, I was arranging this before the petition."

$entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadline

options:
0:catchrelease_fqAccept:"I'll take the job."
5:catchrelease_fqAcceptNoPromise:"I'll try. No promises." (Accept)
10:catchrelease_fqDecline:Decline.

text: "Good. I'll tell the crew we've got somebody working on it. You'll be very welcome when you arrive."
"Try for it. I won't announce the menu until you've got the catch aboard."
"A pity. I'll keep looking. I'll tell the petition committee you were polite. $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName out."

"$entity.catchreleaseFleetRationDays days now. They've added desserts to the petition. Have you got $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk, or do I have to tell them we're still on protein?"

$entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadlineLeft

The galley chief inspects the delivery container by container before waving each one through to prep. Their shoulders finally come down.

"Good. Cold storage, second rack. Knives out. Somebody get the large pans hot."

The galley erupts into motion.

"No. The printer produces everything a human body needs. Ask the medical officer. Ask the captain. Neither of them has to stand here while it's eaten."

The chief looks across the mess.

"I've started putting out condiments we used to use for cleaning. I'd like to stop."

"Night watch gets the same portions as everyone else. I've had to write that on the door."

Something boils over behind the chief.

"Right. Thank you, captain. If you'll excuse me, I've finally got work to do."

id: # fleet quest: scavenger with a dead engine

text: Scavenger with a Dead Engine
Repacking the drive coil

A drive coil aboard $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName needs repacking, but the scavengers have run out of gel. Their technician found an approved substitute made from rendered fish. Suitable species occur nearby; you don't have to catch them in any particular system.
The repair supply request is recorded on the following terms.
"Coil technician aboard the scavenger $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName. We've got a drive repair held up for lack of one consumable."

"We've got the replacement winding in, but there's no packing gel. Can't bring the drive up without it. The yard manual says we can render a substitute from fish."

The technician sends section $entity.catchreleaseFleetManualSection for your inspection. "That's the current edition. We checked."

"We need $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. Those turn up around here, if you've got the gear. The salvage haul will cover $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward."

$entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadline

options:
0:catchrelease_fqAccept:"I'll get what you need."
5:catchrelease_fqAcceptNoPromise:"I'll try. No promises." (Accept)
10:catchrelease_fqDecline:Decline.

0:catchrelease_fqAccept:"First I've heard of it. But I can get you the fish."
5:catchrelease_fqAcceptNoPromise:"No, but I'll see what I can find." (Accept)
10:catchrelease_fqDecline:Decline.
8:catchrelease_fqQuestion:"How does a fish pack a drive coil?"

text: "Good. I'll get the rest of the repair ready. Hail us when you're on your way back."
"It's worth a try. I'll send the manual extract. Have your people check it before you bring anything over; I'd rather not dismantle the coil twice."
"Figured. We'll keep looking for another supply. $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName out."

"The coil still reads $entity.catchreleaseFleetCoilCondition. We're leaving it cold until we've repacked it. Any luck with $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk?"

$entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadlineLeft

Your catch goes down to engineering. Some time later the technician hails to let you hear the drive running. The crew wait through two low-load cycles before anyone speaks.

"Temperatures look right. We'll bring it up slowly. Thank you, Captain."

"Render it, filter the useful fraction, pack it around the winding. The manual gives an eighteen-to-twenty-two percent yield. Good from minus forty to two hundred ten, then two low-load cycles before we trust it."

The technician looks up. "Have you heard of this? Nobody here has tried it."
"It's holding temperature. No leaks or faults so far. I'll put a copy of that page in the repair locker. Thanks for stopping."
A scavenger vessel is holding position with its drive cold. A standard assistance request is running on the local trade band.
Burn Ward
Treating burn casualties

A reactor-space fire aboard $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName left $entity.catchreleaseFleetCasualties crew badly burned. With the synthskin exhausted, the medical officer needs fish skin for temporary dressings. Only fish caught after you accept the request will be fresh enough for the work.
The medical officer's request is recorded on the following terms.
"Thank you for answering. Medical officer, $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName. We had a fire and I have burn casualties."

"$entity.catchreleaseFleetCasualties burned in the reactor space. I used the last of our synthskin on the worst two. The others have gel dressings. I'm changing them as often as I can."

The medical officer moves the pickup away from the beds. "I've used fish skin on frontier postings. Properly prepared, it will hold until we get these people to a hospital."

script: CatchReleaseCMD highlightJobText $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk "Fresh catch, after you accept the request" $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward $entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadline
text:
"I need $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. Fresh catch, after you accept the request, with a capture record I can rely on."

"$entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward. That's authorized. Keep the catch cold and come straight back."

$entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadline

options:
0:catchrelease_fqAccept:"I'll bring you the fish."
5:catchrelease_fqAcceptNoPromise:"I'll try. No promises." (Accept)
10:catchrelease_fqDecline:Decline.

text:
"Thank you. I'm sending our position and a handling note."

The note is two lines long. Keep the catch cold. Leave the skin on.

"Please do what you can."

The handling note arrives: keep the catch cold and leave the skin intact.

"Then we'll keep broadcasting."

The channel closes.

"I'm still changing gel dressings. Have you brought $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk? I'll need the record showing it was caught since you took the job."

$entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadlineLeft

An orderly brings an insulated trolley to receive the catch. The medical officer checks the capture record while the team prepares the skin.

"Bed four first. Have someone stay with him."

By the time your receipt is signed, the first dressing is being applied.

"A miner, burns across most of his back. The supply shuttle was three weeks late. I used what we had, and he walked out of my medbay alive."

The officer turns at a call from one of the beds, then comes back. "I'd use synthskin if I had it, Captain. I don't. My people need covering."
"All $entity.catchreleaseFleetCasualties have proper dressings now. We're arranging a transfer to a hospital. Thank you, Captain. They needed this."
A small trader is broadcasting a distress call with a medical priority code. Scans show fire damage around its reactor section.
Fouled Line
Holding at a fouled breach

Both drones belonging to the fishing boat $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName are stuck beyond $entity.catchreleaseFleetRupture. The skipper is relying on an old remedy: another crew brings aboard a fresh catch from the same rupture. Your catch must come from that rupture after you accept the request.
The skipper's request is recorded on the following terms.
"$entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName. We're a fishing crew and we're stuck. You're the first hull that's stopped."

"Both of them. First one stopped coming back, sent the second to find it. Six hours now. Still answering, won't move."

The skipper sends you the two drone tracks ending inside $entity.catchreleaseFleetRupture. A deckhand passes behind the pickup, counting the crew again.

"Trade says keep your trips short in thin fabric. This one isn't short anymore. Those drones are worth more than the boat, but I can't sit here forever."

script: CatchReleaseCMD highlightJobText $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk $entity.catchreleaseFleetRupture "after you take the job" $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward $entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadline
text:
"There's an old remedy. Another crew fishes the breach and brings a catch aboard us. I've seen it free a fouled line. We need $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk, from $entity.catchreleaseFleetRupture after you take the job. We can pay $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward."

$entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadline

options:
0:catchrelease_fqAccept:"I'll work the breach."
5:catchrelease_fqAcceptNoPromise:"I'll try. No promises." (Accept)
10:catchrelease_fqDecline:Decline.

text:
"Thank you. I'll send the fix and both drone tracks. Give those tracks some room."

The skipper marks them on your chart. "Bring the catch here once you've landed it."
"Burn bright, Captain. I've sent the fix and both tracks. Give our drones room, and bring the catch aboard as soon as you've landed it. It has to come from that breach, after this call."

"Right. We'll keep calling."

The channel closes.

"They're answering, but they won't move. Have you got $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk from $entity.catchreleaseFleetRupture? We're ready to take it aboard."

$entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadlineLeft

A deckhand carries your catch aboard in a sealed tank and sets it down on the bridge.
The skipper logs it against $entity.catchreleaseFleetRupture.

A few minutes later, both drone tracks start moving toward the boat.

"Then we leave them."

The skipper looks at the tracks.

"I keep saying they cost more than the boat. Doesn't mean I ought to lose the boat as well."

"My first skipper did it twice. Both times, the drone came home once the other crew's catch was aboard. Never knew why."

The skipper calls for another position check. "You can call it superstition. Nobody on this boat is going to argue with it today."

"Both drones are back in the rack. One lost a sensor mast, but that we can fix."

The skipper is already plotting a course away from the breach. "Burn bright, captain."
A small fishing boat is holding station at a rupture and broadcasting a distress call. It has not moved since the call began.
Collector's Commission
Waiting

A collector aboard $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName has repeatedly lost specimens to last-minute sales through other brokers. Suspecting a rival buyer, the collector has commissioned you directly to supply the missing entry in an otherwise carefully prepared display.
The private commission is recorded on the following terms.
"Private vessel $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName. I have a collection commission to place, if you are taking work."

"Three deposits, Captain. Three. Each returned just before the transfer, with an apology and no specimen. I do not want another apology."

The collector turns the pickup toward an empty display tank. An engraved nameplate has been fixed below the glass.

"I want $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. Someone is buying them out from under me. So I am dispensing with brokers. Obtain one yourself and bring it directly here. $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward. The tank has been ready for two years."

$entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadline

options:
0:catchrelease_fqAccept:"I'll take the commission."
5:catchrelease_fqAcceptNoPromise:"I'll try. No promises." (Accept)
10:catchrelease_fqDecline:Decline.
7:catchrelease_fqExtraQuestion:"You've kept the tank ready for two years?"
8:catchrelease_fqQuestion:"What makes you think it's one buyer?"

text: "Very good. I will transmit the collection entry and receiving requirements."
"Take care over it. I'd rather have the specimen than an assurance. I'm sending the receiving instructions."
"Then I have wasted another call. Very well, Captain. Do put me in touch with someone willing to take the commission."

"Have you obtained $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk? Please let me know before you transfer it. I would like to receive it myself."

$entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadlineLeft

The collector receives the container personally and takes it to the display tank.
They compare the holding temperatures, set the acclimation flow and wait beside the tank until the transfer is complete.

The specimen settles behind the glass beneath the engraved nameplate.

The collector sends three transactions, dated $entity.catchreleaseFleetBrokerDates.

"Carthen & Vale. Morrow Exchange. Silex Acquisitions. Different brokers, almost identical apologies. The last one suggested I consider a different specimen. A different specimen! As though I had engraved the nameplate for my amusement."

"I cannot prove it is one buyer. I have, however, had enough of being sniped."

The collector stands beside the tank long after the transfer crew have left.

"Look at it. Whoever was buying all of these can keep them. Mine is the best."

The pickup is turned so you can admire it too.

The collector turns the pickup toward the tank. Its lights and filters are running beneath an engraved nameplate.

"Eighteen point five degrees. Ten-hour display cycle. I've had it ready all this time. I test the holding conditions every morning."
Settling a Bet
Arguing

Two watches aboard $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName have turned a disagreement over survey returns into a substantial bet. Their captain wants a pair of matching specimens to compare with the records and put an end to it. The fish must be the same species and meet the wager's other terms.
The wager has the following terms.

"Scavenger fleet $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName. Captain speaking. I've got an argument between two watches that's gone on long enough. They put money on it, naturally.
If you fish, you might be able to settle it for us."

"It started with a bottle."

The captain sends two survey logs from the same fishing ground.

"First watch reckons these returns prove there's a run. Second watch reckons they got lucky twice and wrote a report about it."

"Now there's money involved. Enough that I don't want to settle it by telling them both to shut up."

"I need $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. Two of the same species, so we can compare them with the returns. The pot will cover $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward."

"I've forbidden any more betting. That hasn't improved the atmosphere."

$entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadline

# the label needs a colon, which the Options column cannot hold

text:
"Good. I'll send the logs with the order."

The captain pauses to address someone off-screen. "No, hiring someone doesn't void it. We agreed on outside verification."
"Good enough. I'll send both logs so you know what we're comparing it with."
"All right. I'll deal with them. $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName out."

"Now they're disputing the wording of the bet. We wrote it down at the time. Have you got $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk? I'd like to put an end to it."

$entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadlineLeft

A couple of crew from each watch come forward to inspect the catch.

There is some muttering before the captain cuts them off and checks the specimens against the logs. "That's enough. Pay out the bets."

The captain authorizes the transfer to your account.

"They've both tried explaining the readings to me. Repeatedly. I can tell them who's on watch, but I can't make those logs prove what they caught. Bring us specimens to compare and they'll have to accept the result. That much they did agree to."

"Paid out. Both watches signed for it."

Someone speaks off-screen.

"No, we're not taking bets on whether the sample was representative."

The captain turns back. "Thank you, captain. I'll handle the rest."

"Neither. You're bringing the specimens. We compare them with the logs and settle it here."

"The fee is the same whichever watch wins. I insisted on that before calling you."

text:
Your comms officer picks up a personal beacon running on emergency power. It leads to a prefabricated surface cache.

Someone has made a living compartment out of one of the storage bays. Its occupant is thin, dirty, and already waving at the camera.

A garbled transmission calls out almost immediately.

"You came back! Please take me aboard, $PlayerSirOrMadam, I beg of you!"

text:
"Missed the boat."

He sees your expression and hurries on.

"We were doing a transfer. Skipper thought I was on the tender. Tender thought I was back aboard. Both had the same manifest, so both signed and left."

He gestures at the compartment behind him.

"I waited for them to notice. Then I thought I'd better see what was in the cache."

text:
"Fishing crew. Worked with the Fisherman's boats."

He digs out an old comm unit and reads your officer a fleet handshake.

"Try that when you find them. Trawlers, usually, out past the settled traffic. Tell the Fisherman who you've got aboard. He'll know me."

You order bombardment of the coordinates the beacon is broadcasting from. 

It falls silent with a single shot.

He accepts before you finish the sentence.

Your personnel officer finds a spare berth.

The Fisherman answers from a worktable. He puts down a dismantled control unit and wipes his hands before taking the call.

"Evening, Captain. What can I do for you?"

"Captain. Back with a catch?"

A crewman passes behind the Fisherman carrying a sealed crate. By the time he reaches the hatch his hands are empty. The Fisherman waits while your comms officer clears the channel.

"Evening." The Fisherman's voice comes through before the comm indicator turns green. When the picture arrives, he is pouring a drink into a battered mug.

"Go ahead. I'm listening."

The Fisherman is watching someone work out of view when the link opens. "Easy with that. Set it down first."

Metal strikes a deck plate on your left audio channel, though the trawler lies to starboard. He turns back to the pickup. "Sorry, Captain. You were saying?"

"Try $catchreleaseRumorSystem. The catch hasn't been running as hard there lately. You might find it a bit easier to land something you've been having trouble with."

text: The lamps are already dark. The patrol has the earlier sensor return on display and proceeds with the stop.

"Power down the lights, Captain. Whatever you're doing is interfering with the inhabited approaches at $entity.catchrelease_lampWhere. Shut it down and take the operation elsewhere. This is your warning."

"Hegemony Navy. Shut the device down."

$PersonRank $personName has your sensor return and the traffic plot side by side. "Unlicensed high-energy operation inside a protected navigation volume.
You have one warning."

"Kill the lights. Now."

"Corporate security. Power down your equipment. It's interfering with local operations."

An unauthorized-operation notice appears on your comms console. "If you wish to apply for authorization, do so before switching it back on."

"Extinguish it."

$PersonRank $personName looks past your bridge image toward the lamps.

"You were not given creation to cut at until something answers."

The traffic plot remains open.

"There are crews in those approaches, captain. Put the machine away from them."

The channel opens on a $manOrWoman already shouting.

"Kill it! Kill the lamp!"

$HeOrShe stabs a finger toward the sensor image.

"You wound God's work with Moloch's tools so you can drag supper through it, and you call that trade?"

Someone behind $himOrHer is shouting too.

"Extinguish it. Jettison it. Or we will do both for you."

"Kill the lights."

$personName points at a traffic plot. "You are lighting up half our scopes and upsetting people who pay us specifically not to be upset.
Do it somewhere emptier."

"Cease operation by order of the Sindrian Diktat. Your apparatus is interfering with a navigation volume under Sindrian authority."

$PersonRank $personName waits. "Shut it down, Captain. I would prefer to record that you complied with the first instruction."

"League patrol. Power down the equipment. Local navigation restrictions cover industrial operations too, Captain. You'll need to take the fishing somewhere else. We're letting you off with a warning."

"Hey. Lights off."

$personName looks at the sensor plot. "I don't know what you've built. I know every instrument near $entity.catchrelease_lampWhere noticed it.
Take it somewhere nobody lives."
"You've had the warning." The previous incident sits open beside the new one. "$entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS credits. Pay it and shut the rig down."
"You were warned about operating that device. The fine is $entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS credits. Pay it and power down."

"We've recorded a second incident. This one carries an assessment of $entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS credits."

$PersonRank $personName sends the notice. "Further operation will result in inspection and seizure of all catch aboard. I suggest you read it before we have to send a team."

"You were asked once."

The first warning remains open beside the new incident.

"A warning is mercy when it is heard. Ignored, it becomes indulgence."

"The fine is $entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS credits."

"Pay it. Extinguish the lamps. Do not make another crew carry the cost of your choice."

"You kept it!"

The speaker is red-faced in the pickup.

"Of course you kept it. Moloch hands you a knife for creation and you haggle over the handle."

The figure flashes onto the channel.

"$entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS credits. Pay it if numbers are the only language you still understand."

"Then kill the lamp. Next time we come aboard."
"We asked nicely. Now it's $entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS credits. And turn the lights off. You're paying for the trouble you've caused, not permission to keep doing it."
"The order to cease operation remains in force. You will pay $entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS credits and shut down the device. If you operate it again, expect an inspection party."

"Second recorded instance. $entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS credits."

$PersonRank $personName closes the first notice and opens another. "The third provision authorizes inspection and seizure. I'd rather not spend my afternoon invoking it.
Pay the fine and shut the rig down."
"You again." $personName puts the figure on-screen. "$entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS. Lights off. I'd like this to be the last time I learn something new about fishing."
"Power down and prepare for inspection. We're seizing all the catch aboard, including packed crates. Have your cargo records ready and keep your crew clear of the team."

"Hegemony Navy. Heave to. Prepare to be boarded."

The officer does not read the warning history back to you. "You ignored the warning and the fine. We are inspecting the rig and seizing all catch aboard, including packed crates.
Cut the lights."

"The previous notices have been insufficient, Captain. Stand by for boarding."

A shuttle separates from the formation. "All catch aboard is subject to seizure, including packed crates. Power down and have your records ready. Your cooperation will keep this from becoming a security incident."

"Power it down."

"You were warned, then fined. You have continued to put this work before the safety of every soul in those approaches."

The order is signed.

"We are coming aboard. What you brought back while using those lamps will not remain with you."

"Drives cold! Lamps cold!"

The speaker is close enough to the pickup for the image to shake with each word.

"We are coming aboard for what you dragged out under Moloch's light."

A weapon is shoved into view from somewhere behind $himOrHer.

"Touch a control and we'll count that as your answer."

"All right, captain. You've had the cheap versions." A boarding shuttle separates from the formation. "Lights off. Hold open."

The speaker glances past the camera, then back. "And don't make me put a price on resisting."
"Prepare to be boarded. Your equipment will be inspected and all catch aboard seized, including packed crates. Shut it down now. I will not repeat the order while our people are crossing."

"We're proceeding to inspection, Captain. Power down. The team will need your records, and they'll seize all catch aboard, including packed crates. I'll send the authorization so you know what to expect."

$personName has the boarding authorization ready.

"I told you I didn't want to learn more about this. Apparently I do."

"Shut it down. We'll need your cargo records, and we're taking all the catch aboard, including packed crates."

"You've repeatedly ignored orders to stop operating that device. We're authorized to engage."

The other ships begin their approach.

"Hegemony Navy. Further operation of the prohibited device is confirmed. Engagement authorized."

The formation begins to spread before the officer closes the link.
"Your case has been referred to corporate security for armed intervention. We gave you several opportunities to stop operating the device, Captain. The matter is no longer open to negotiation."

$PersonRank $personName is not alone at the screen this time, and nobody behind $himOrHer is speaking.

"We asked. We fined. We took what you had taken. And here it is again, burning over people."

"Ludd forgive you. We will not."

The link closes.

The channel opens to shouting.

"There! There it is again! Moloch's lantern!"

The speaker wipes spittle from the pickup with the heel of a hand.

"You cut at God's creation for meat and credits and still you light it again?"

Someone behind $himOrHer screams, "Break it!"

"No more bargains. Break the lamps. Break the hands that light them."

The link cuts. The Path ships accelerate.

"That's enough. We keep telling you to stop, and you keep turning them on. Let's see you do it without a ship."

The pirate formation accelerates toward your fleet.

"You have repeatedly defied a direct order of the Sindrian Diktat. Force is authorized."

Weapons come online across the formation.
"Local command has reviewed the previous stops and authorized engagement. We are done discussing the regulations, Captain."

"I don't have much choice here, Captain. We've ordered you to stop often enough."

The channel closes. Your sensors officer reports weapons coming online across the other fleet.

The fisher overlays two survey charts. The same rupture sits on opposite sides of a lease boundary.

"My filed chart. Their new survey. Guess which one the security contractor is using."

The traffic record shows $catchreleaseCampMany holding at the disputed site in $catchreleaseCampWhere.

"The claims office won't decide while there are hired guns on the marker. The hired guns won't move until the office decides. I'd like you to interrupt that arrangement."

"Get them off the rupture, then bring me $catchreleaseAsk from that exact spot. Any qualifying catch taken after we agree the job. I need the retrieval record for the claim."

"$catchreleaseDeadline The payment is $catchreleaseReward, once the site is clear and the catch is here."

text:
"Try talking to them first. They're being paid to sit there; they may be willing to be paid to leave."

The fisher sends both charts and the fleet code.

"I'd prefer to get this settled without more wreckage in the claim area."
$HeOrShe returns to the claim form and attaches the second survey chart again.

"No change. The contractor won't move and the claims office won't decide. Have you had any luck with them?"

The fisher marks the rupture again. "$catchreleaseAsk, from that exact spot since you took the job. $catchreleaseDeadlineLeft"

$HeOrShe attaches the retrieval record to the claim. The disputed boundary disappears from $hisOrHer working chart.

"That's evidence I can use."

The fisher answers after checking the doorway.

"Captain. Have they gone?"

A fisher sits with the door in view. A scorched drone-rack isolator rests on the table beside an untouched drink.
A licensed fisher sits facing the door with a damaged power coupler beside the licence slate. Each time the door opens, the inspection of the coupler stops.

text:
"Pathers. They came to preach. Then they cut power to the drone rack."

The fisher puts a burnt component on the table.

"One of them stood on the launch gantry yesterday and said we were feeding Moloch through a wound in creation. Said the next time we worked the rupture, they'd bring rifles."

The transponder record shows $catchreleaseCampMany in $catchreleaseCampWhere.

"Get them away from the boats. I don't care how."

"Bring me $catchreleaseAsk from the same rupture, too. It has to be a catch from after we agree the job. I want to know the spot can still be worked before I send anyone back."

"$catchreleaseDeadline I'll pay $catchreleaseReward when they're gone and you've brought it in."
options:

text:
The fisher checks the door before sending the camp coordinates and transponder record.

"How you move them is your business. Just get them away from the boats."
The fisher nods and deletes the transfer request. The damaged component goes back into a tool bag.

"We've repaired the rack. Nobody will take a boat out while they're there."

$catchreleaseDeadlineLeft

"I've had word they left. Can you bring me $catchreleaseAsk from that rupture? Caught since you took the job. I'd like to see the retrieval record before the boats go out."

$catchreleaseDeadlineLeft

The fisher checks the retrieval record and sends a launch order to the waiting boats.

Someone at the yard is already signing off the repaired rack.

"This spot's off limits."

The pirate glances toward the rupture. "We found it empty. Now it isn't.
Turn around, or transfer $entity.catchrelease_campBribeDGS credits and we'll find another quiet place."

"You are entering a contracted exclusion zone. Alter course."

$PersonRank $personName sends a file number.

"If you've come about the fishing, the relocation price is $entity.catchrelease_campBribeDGS credits. Otherwise there's nothing to discuss."

The $manOrWoman on the screen is already shouting before the link stabilizes.

"Back! Keep that machine away from the rupture!"

Someone behind $himOrHer raises a weapon.

"You lower Moloch's iron into places no human hand should reach, scratch at God's creation for meat and coin, and call it fishing!"

The payment figure appears.

"$entity.catchrelease_campBribeDGS credits and we leave. Do not mistake that for permission."

"You've come about the fishing spot."

Whoever answers checks your fleet before continuing. "We're using it. You want us somewhere else, $entity.catchrelease_campBribeDGS credits makes somewhere else worth the trouble."

"Well. Somebody actually came out."

The pirate looks toward the rupture. "Nice bit of empty space. No patrols, no customs, no traffic unless somebody wants the fishing."

"$entity.catchrelease_campBribeDGS buys us another quiet place. Otherwise this one's occupied."

"Our contract is to deny access to the site. The client's name is confidential."

$PersonRank $personName sends you the relocation clause.

"$entity.catchrelease_campBribeDGS credits. At that price I can justify leaving. Below it, I'm being paid to stay."

The $manOrWoman on the screen is standing now. Somebody behind $himOrHer is shouting over a weapon check.

"You came back for the fishing."

$HeOrShe points toward the rupture.

"We have watched crews bring their machines here and lower them into places no human hand should reach. You claw at God's work for appetite and coin, then call it a trade."

The payment figure appears.

"$entity.catchrelease_campBribeDGS credits buys our absence. It does not make you clean."

text:
You ask how long they intend to hold a fixed position that every displaced fishing crew knows about. Your fleet has found them. Other captains can do the same, and sooner or later one will prefer shooting to negotiation.

There is a pause while the person on the screen confers with someone out of view.

"We were moving on anyway."

The formation begins to come about.

"Yes, Captain, you did."

He moves the rupture marker into the centre of the display. "Have you had a look at the fishing here yet?"

text:
"You'll be fishing in places like this. I'd sooner you tried it now than on a contract halfway out of the Core. If your catch won't keep its shape, you'll know the rig hasn't necessarily gone wrong."

He points out the area he wants you to work. "Bring me the $catchreleaseTarget. I'll have a look before you start taking the machinery apart."
options:

catchrelease_fisherBack:"All right. I'll get on with it."

text: "It can. That's why I told you to make it a short visit. You've got the gear and you know what you're after. If the crew start giving you cause for concern, leave the fish."

text: "I'm buying for somebody else, so I can't do much about them. Anything the order doesn't specify is up to you. If you're thinking of a substitution, check the written terms before you go to the trouble of catching it."

"Because it's my menu! Because the customers have booked for it! Because if I change one more thing the head waiter will come back here and explain cooking to me!"

The chef takes a breath. "Look. I can cook it. You can catch it. We ought to be able to manage between us."
"Precisely." The factor smiles. "Even with conservative estimates."
"I haven't approached them formally. It would be premature without stock."
"You will be paid when you deliver, Captain. I have the funds. My arrangements aren't your security."

"We keep images and measurements alongside the retrieval logs. A specimen can be very useful even when we can't safely display it. I've got gaps in both collections, so don't worry about bringing a mixture. We'll find room."
options:
catchrelease_jobAccept:Agree to supply the collection.
catchrelease_jobDecline:Decline.

text:
The researcher shows you two measurements of the same specimen. They don't agree.

"I recalibrated and got a third result. My supervisor suggested discarding the first one. On what grounds? I followed the same procedure for all three. I need more specimens before I can get anywhere with this."

"Captain, I am thinking two videos. Two reveals. First we give them the beautiful one. Then you bring me something from low-coherence space and we see how long it takes chat to decide I've been replaced."

$HeOrShe glances at the lens. "Chat. You cannot accuse me of faking footage I haven't filmed yet."

"First specimen, first payment. Then I'll give you the second order and the new offer. And you have to sit in the same chair. Last time I moved the chair, they said we'd switched studios."

"Chat. The captain has just noticed the camera. Look at that. That's the thumbnail."

$HeOrShe reaches past you to adjust a lamp. "Yes, Captain, we're recording. Please keep looking exactly like that. No, don't look at the lens. You were doing it perfectly a moment ago."

options: -10:catchrelease_intro_fourJumps:"I just left you in another system."

text: "Then it isn't a complete survey. We'd lose the classification, explain the omission, and still claim expenses for the time we've spent trying to fill it. The captain would rather we finished. So would I."

"Good company on a long passage. Thorough about the work. Thorough about other people's work, too, which could be less welcome."

The convoy master looks back at the will. "They would have checked this clause before departure. I should have done the same."
"I wanted you to know how to bring it back before we got into what it might be. Ask your questions, Captain. We're not going anywhere yet."
